manimR

manimR is a native R port of Manim Community, the animation engine for explanatory math videos. Scenes, mobjects, animations, LaTeX, text, graphing, 3D and camera tools follow the Python API closely, so Manim examples translate almost line by line. Rendering is done in R with grid on an offscreen ragg device, and frames are streamed to ffmpeg.

The website, https://adamrsophie.github.io/manimR/, has the full reference and a set of articles that show every feature with rendered videos:

  • Getting started and Coming from Python manim
  • Mobjects and geometry, Animations, Updaters and value trackers
  • Text, math and tables, Graphs, plots and coordinate systems, Cameras and 3D scenes, Colors, images, SVG and point clouds
  • Rendering, configuration and output, RStudio, knitr, Quarto and Shiny, Math and utility functions

The introduction is also installed with the package: vignette("manimR").

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/manimR")

System requirements:

  • ffmpeg for video output (MP4, GIF, WebM, MOV).
  • A LaTeX distribution with dvisvgm for Tex() and MathTex() (for example tinytex::install_tinytex() plus tinytex::tlmgr_install("dvisvgm")).
  • Optionally the typst command line compiler for Typst() and MathTypst(); point to it with manim_config(typst = "/path/to/typst").

Run manim_check() to see what was found.

A first scene 

library(manimR)

SquareToCircle <- R6::R6Class("SquareToCircle", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    circle <- Circle()$set_fill(PINK, opacity = 0.5)
    square <- Square()$rotate(PI / 4)
    self$play(Create(square))
    self$play(Transform(square, circle))
    self$play(FadeOut(square))
  })
)

render(SquareToCircle, quality = "l", preview = TRUE)

The functional form is shorter for quick experiments:

render(function(self) {
  eq <- MathTex("e^{i\\pi}", "+", "1", "=", "0")
  self$play(Write(eq))
  self$play(Indicate(eq[3]))
}, quality = "l")

Translating Manim code

Python manim manimR
Circle(radius=2, color=RED) Circle(radius = 2, color = RED)
sq.shift(LEFT).scale(2) sq$shift(LEFT)$scale(2)
self.play(sq.animate.rotate(PI)) self$play(sq$animate$rotate(PI))
group[0] group[1] (indices start at 1)
len(group) length(group)
VGroup(*mobs) VGroup(mobs) or VGroup(a, b, c)
t2c={"x": RED} t2c = list(x = RED)
rate_func=smooth rate_func = smooth_rate or rate_functions$smooth (avoids masking stats::smooth())
rate_functions.ease_in_sine rate_functions$ease_in_sine (or ease_in_sine)
from manim.utils.color import X11 X11_COLORS or color$X11 (avoids masking grDevices::X11())
config.frame_height, frame.top config$frame_height, manim_frame$top (avoids masking graphics::frame())
with tempconfig({...}): tempconfig(list(...), { ... })
ManimColor("#FF0000").darker() ManimColor("#FF0000")$darker()
clip(a, 0, 1) clip_value(a, 0, 1) (avoids masking graphics::clip())
class S(Scene): def construct(self): S <- R6::R6Class("S", inherit = Scene, public = list(construct = function() ...))
manim -pql file.py S render_file("file.R", "S", quality = "l", preview = TRUE)

Every constructor Foo() has an exported R6 generator FooClass for subclassing, for example R6::R6Class("MyShape", inherit = VMobjectClass, ...), including the classes upstream defines only to preset arguments (MathTableClass, ReplacementTransformClass, and so on). Constructors show the full argument list of their class, so RStudio’s completion lists the same arguments as Manim’s documentation. Class wide defaults work like Manim’s set_default(): set_default(Text, font_size = 60).

Every public name of from manim import * has an R counterpart; the only renames are the ones above, made so no export masks a base R function (upstream’s choose() is base::choose(), and its unit module’s members Pixels, Percent(), Degrees and Munits are exported directly). tests/testthat/test-api-coverage.R checks this against the upstream source, for every exported name and every public method of every exported class. Colors are hex strings; ManimColor() wraps one when you need upstream’s color methods. As upstream, a misspelled argument (Circle(raduis = 2)) or setting (manim_config(qualty = "l")) is an error.

Two exports share names with other packages: Matrix() and MatrixClass (also in the Matrix package) and Cross() (also in purrr as cross(), a different case). Attach manimR last, or write manimR::Matrix().

Rendering options

render() and manim_config() take Manim 0.22’s settings: quality ("l", "m", "h", "p", "k"), transparent, background_color, frame_rate, media_dir and the rest (see ?manim_config). format chooses the artifact: "auto" (MP4, or MOV when transparent; a scene with no animations is saved as its last frame), "mp4", "mov", "webm", "gif", "png" (only the last frame; save_last_frame = TRUE means the same), "png-sequence" (every frame) or "none"; dry_run = TRUE renders without writing files. Output goes to media/videos/<module>/<quality>/<Scene>.mp4 and media/images/<module>/ like Manim; the media folder is in the R session’s temporary directory unless you set media_dir (for example manim_config(media_dir = "media")), while manim_cli() uses ./media as Manim’s command line does. The directory settings (video_dir, images_dir, partial_movie_dir, tex_dir, …) take the same {media_dir}, {module_name}, {quality} and {scene_name} placeholders (get_dir() resolves them). A manim.cfg file is read with digest_config_file(), and the command line reads one in the working directory.

Scenes can be split with self$next_section("name"); with save_sections = TRUE each section is also written to its own video under sections/ with a JSON index, and next_section(skip_animations = TRUE) skips a section while you work on later ones. self$add_sound() and self$play(..., subcaption = "...") add audio and an .srt subtitle file.

As in Manim, each play is written to its own partial movie file, named by a hash of the renderer, the encoder settings, the camera, the animations and the scene’s mobjects (including the values updaters use), and the files are joined into the movie. Rendering again reuses the files of unchanged plays; disable_caching = TRUE (--disable_caching) renders everything, flush_cache = TRUE (--flush_cache) empties the cache first, and max_files_cached (default 100) limits its size. video_codec, pixel_format and video_encoder_options choose how the segments are encoded.

scene_frame(MyScene, t = 2.5) renders the single frame at 2.5 seconds without writing a video, and plot() shows it.

From a terminal:

Rscript -e 'manimR::manim_cli()' scenes.R SquareToCircle -ql -p

The command line takes all of manim render’s options (-ql, -p, -s, -t, -a, -o FILE, -n N,M, -r W,H, --fps, --format, --save_sections, --dry_run, --media_dir, -c manim.cfg, --encoder-option crf=18, …) and the subcommands checkhealth, cfg show|write|export, init project|scene, plugins -l and cache clear; see ?manim_cli.

RStudio

The package installs RStudio addins (Addins menu):

  • Render scene at cursor: renders the scene defined at or above the cursor and plays it in the Viewer pane.
  • Render all scenes in file.
  • Preview last frame: renders only the final frame, which is much faster.
  • Insert scene template.
  • Render scene in background: renders as an RStudio background job and shows the result when it is done.
  • Render with options: a dialog to choose scene, quality, format and transparency.

Set options(manimR.addin_quality = "m") to change the quality the quick addins use. plot(mobject) draws any mobject in the Plots pane.

Shiny

manimOutput() and renderManim() show a scene in a Shiny app and render it again when the inputs it uses change:

output$scene <- renderManim({
  n <- input$sides
  function(self) self$play(Create(RegularPolygon(n = n)))
})

Other R graphics and data

as_mobject() turns a ggplot2 chart, a grid grob or base graphics into a vector mobject that can be animated, and GraphClass$from_igraph() builds a Graph() from an igraph graph.

R Markdown and Quarto

A manim knitr engine renders scenes inside documents:

```{manim, scene = "SquareToCircle", quality = "l"}
SquareToCircle <- R6::R6Class("SquareToCircle", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() self$play(Create(Circle()))))
```

HTML output embeds the video, PDF output the last frame and other formats (GitHub Markdown, Word) a GIF. The same engine works in Quarto documents that use the knitr engine. In an r chunk, the value of render() is embedded the same way when it is printed.

Differences from Python manim

  • Every scene renders with the Cairo style renderer (CairoRenderer), which draws with grid on a ragg device instead of pycairo, so the camera’s Cairo context helpers have no counterpart. manim_config(renderer = "opengl") is accepted but renders the same way. The OpenGL point clouds (DotCloud, TrueDot, OpenGLPMobject) are drawn as round dots like upstream’s shader draws them, and the other OpenGL mobject classes (OpenGLCircle, OpenGLSurface, …) are subclasses of their Cairo counterparts. The GPU pipeline itself (shaders, the OpenGL camera and window) is not ported.
  • Interactive mode (scene$interactive_embed(), embed(), interact()) opens a Shiny window instead of upstream’s OpenGL window: it shows the live scene, takes the same key and mouse events (orbit, pan, zoom, r, q, set_key_function()) and has a code box in place of the IPython shell.
  • Plugins are R packages whose DESCRIPTION sets Config/manimR/plugin: true (see get_plugins()), not Python entry points.
  • Text() uses system fonts through textshaping and systemfonts instead of Pango, so glyph shapes and metrics follow the installed fonts. MarkupText() wraps and justifies lines at upstream’s Pango layout width.
  • Boolean operations (Union(), Intersection(), Difference(), Exclusion()) use the polyclip package, so their results are made of straight segments.
  • Code() highlights with Pygments, as upstream, when Python with the pygments module is installed; without it, a built in tokenizer highlights R and Python.
  • Video segments are encoded in the R process, one at a time; max_inflight_encoders and encoder_queue_size are accepted but have no effect.
  • Copy mobjects with $copy(); R6’s $clone() keeps the original’s id.
  • ImplicitFunction() traces contours with grDevices::contourLines() instead of an adaptive quadtree.
  • Graph layouts, including "planar", are native ports of the networkx algorithms, so igraph is not required. Where networkx picks an arbitrary element of a set, the first vertex is used, so a planar drawing can differ from networkx while staying free of crossings.
  • In 3D scenes the camera’s frame_center is subtracted once (upstream subtracts it twice). Shaded strokes color each drawn segment from the shading gradient instead of filling a gradient, which looks the same at the thin strokes surfaces use.
  • Images in formats other than PNG (JPEG, GIF, WebP and so on) are read through ffmpeg.
  • Index valued helpers keep upstream’s 0 based numbers where they are arithmetic rather than positions in an R list: integer_interpolate() and the get_3d_vmob_*() corner indices. Labels and positions that index R objects (index_labels(), earclip_triangulation()) start at 1.
  • subdivide_bezier() splits curves of degree 4 or more at i/n, as its upstream documentation states; upstream’s code for those degrees splits elsewhere. Manim itself only uses cubic curves.
  • override_animation() and override_animate() replace the decorators of the same names: override_animation(MyClass, "FadeIn", function(...) ...).
  • ZoomedScene redraws the zoomed region as vector graphics instead of copying pixels.
  • Arguments named function in Python are called func (a reserved word in R), and indices such as axis numbers start at 1.

Fidelity tests

The test suite compares points, positions, colors, timings and LaTeX output against reference data produced by Python manim (data-raw/*.py regenerate the fixtures in tests/testthat/fixtures/). Geometry, alignment, transforms, partial curves, rate functions, graphing, 3D shapes, camera projections, graph layouts, matrices and tables match upstream to within numerical precision.

Acknowledgments

manimR is a port of Manim Community, created by the Manim Community developers on top of Grant Sanderson’s original manim for 3Blue1Brown. Its design, algorithms and examples follow their work, which is gratefully acknowledged. Manim Community is released under the MIT license. The graph layouts are translated from NetworkX (BSD 3 clause license) and the polygon triangulation from earcut.hpp (ISC license).
